Back in June, we reported three cases in which apps linked to banks under U.S. sanctions on Russia bypassed review and made it onto the App Store. Two months on, fresh cases have surfaced, with one even climbing to the top of the iPhone App Store.

The latest example is K8CHEN PRO. On the App Store, its listing disguises it as a kitchen design app powered by AR technology.

The moment you open the app, the disguise falls apart. The privacy policy it links to was generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator" — which in itself may be a red flag.

In short, this app is unmistakably a client for T-Bank. What I find intriguing is how apps like these keep slipping past App Store review.

Once these apps gain traction and climb the App Store rankings, it becomes obvious they should never have been allowed on the store in the first place — a puzzling state of affairs.

The other two cases mentioned in June can be found here and here.

Make the most of your Apple products
